lead.title: CSL licenses lixudebart, Swiss biotech Alentis's anti-Claudin-1, for $355M upfront and up to $1.5B
lead.deck: CSL pays $355M upfront and up to $1.2B in commercial milestones in exchange for 55% of global profits on the candidate, now in Phase II (RENAL trial in ANCA-associated vasculitis with glomerulonephritis); Phase II trials are planned in FSGS and primary sclerosing cholangitis, and a Phase III in vasculitis. An upfront this size on a Phase II asset validates the Claudin-1 target in fibro-inflammatory disease.

milestone.title: Nanexa (Sweden) licenses its PharmaShell platform to Novo Nordisk for up to €1.165B
milestone.summary: Novo can apply the ultra-thin inorganic coating, deposited by atomic layer deposition, to peptides in up to five programs (obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiometabolic), moving from weekly to monthly or quarterly injections; €615M in upfront and milestone payments, €1.165B including sales milestones, plus royalties. Announced in late September, following a first deal with Moderna in December 2025.
milestone.why: A second major license for the platform in ten months: duration of action is becoming a differentiator in incretins, and formulation technologies are a more capital-efficient way in than new molecules.

deal.thesis: The Paris biotech, which applies AI to the design of genomic medicines, closes a Series B led by AVP to accelerate its development.

brefsEurope.title: Forbion raises €2.3B across two funds, Growth Opportunities IV and Ventures Fund VIII
brefsEurope.summary: Europe's largest life-sciences-only venture investor (€7.5B under management) counts MN, PGGM, KfW Capital and Eli Lilly among its LPs; capacity to back up to 30 young companies.

brefsIntl.title: KymaThera raises $80M Series B led by Alta Partners for its oral PI3Kα inhibitor K-1728
brefsIntl.summary: Foresite Capital and Venrock take part; first Phase I patients targeted for Q4 2026 after IND-enabling studies: a preclinical-round comparable for European precision oncology.

word.definition: A formulation injected once that slowly releases the active ingredient over weeks or months, replacing daily or weekly dosing.

parts.label: Matrix / coating
parts.role: the hourglass: polymer or inorganic layer that slows release

parts.label: Depot under the skin
parts.role: the reservoir formed at the injection site

how.t: A single dose is injected under the skin or into muscle as a depot.
The matrix or coating dissolves gradually, on a profile set by its composition and thickness.
The active ingredient enters the blood at a controlled rate for 1 to 6 months.

word.why: Less adherence burden and steadier concentrations: formulations extend the commercial life of known molecules and attract big pharma, as the Novo Nordisk–Nanexa license in obesity shows.

startups.name: Nanexa
startups.use: PharmaShell platform (atomic layer deposition coating); Moderna (Dec 2025) and Novo Nordisk (Sept 2026) licenses for sustained-release peptides

startups.name: Medincell
startups.use: Subcutaneous depots based on a resorbable PLA polymer releasing over 1 to 6 months; UZEDY (risperidone) marketed with Teva
